chapter: New York, church bands and early training
title: Popular tunes, stock arrangements and church music
summary: Briggs recalls the popular numbers of the time played as one-steps at dance schools, and distinguishes the church band's sacred repertoire; he joined the 369th at sixteen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, what kind of music was being played in New York at that time?
Medleys -- you're talking about jazz music?
Well, in general, 'cause
Briggs

there couldn't have been much jazz. You see the thing is, the point is, I mentioned this number, "I Wish I Could Shimmy Like My Sister Kate," and, "How Are You Gonna Keep Them Down on the Farm," and things like that.
Those were the numbers that was more or less popular, you see, popular numbers. When we played at the dance school, we played them as one-steps.
Well, you had arrangements of these?
Oh, yes. Yes, we had stock arrangements.
And you had "Sister Kate," even then?
Yes, yes.
Yes, yes. No, wait a minute. That was after 1912, a little after 1912.
A little after.
Briggs
After 1912. I was more or less, say around about fifteen then.
I see.

I was fifteen. And I'm just talking and talking and talking -- When I played "Sister Kate," I was fifteen and a half, almost sixteen, 'cause I became a member of the 369th when I was sixteen, and that's when Lt. Simpson was commissioned to sign musicians to replace Jim Europe's band leaving.
Okay, let me get that straight. I'm a little confused about what actually is happening here. So, the bands at that time, like your church band, were they playing ragtime arrangements.
Not in the church.
Not in the church band.
We played what you call, "church music".
Briggs
I see.
Church music.
But you would play in the church?
Yes, I played in church as well.
Right.
You had to. You had brass, you had trombones, you had trumpets, you had violins, many violins, violas, and everything else.
You know. A church -- you know, a regular orchestra, organist -- you have an organist.
But this wasn't in church on Sunday.
Church on Sunday, you had it with the choir.
Right.
You had choir rehearsals and things.
